feature: An animated icon told as a little story
summary: Asking for an icon that tells a story of several beats now always makes a moving icon, even when your words never say animated or have a typo in it. Before it lands, Ask looks at frames of its own motion and mends any beat it could not see, and its row says if it had to leave one out. Since the last pass it plans about 30 seconds quicker, no longer sends back keys it already fixed, and sees where each moving part sits at each beat.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Close every window, then type your sentence into the New window: make an animated trash icon where the lid opens and some trash is thrown in, bouncing off the lid and causing it to close. Press Create.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Space and watch the lid open, the paper ball come in by the lid, and the lid shut; the timeline shows Ball, Impact and Lid keyed on their own.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Ask for: make an animated heart icon where the heart beats twice and then breaks. Watch the line under the request say Checking the motion, then Fixing the motion.
Open the heart's reel to see it play as a browser plays the file.
Open the reel to see the exported SVG playing as a browser plays it.
Try it without the word: make a trash icon where the lid opens and some trash is thrown in, bouncing off the lid and causing it to close.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Check a still stays still: make an icon of a balloon popping. It should be a still icon, as before.
Choose Copy SVG and paste the file into a browser: it loops.

evaluate: Does every request you meant as moving now move, including ones without the word animated?
Does a one-action icon you meant as a still (a bell ringing, a door opening) still come out still?
In the trash reel, can you tell the trash bounces off the lid and that is what shuts it?
When Ask leaves a beat out, is the row's line ('Left out the bounce; it could not be planned.') enough to know what to ask for next?
Does the heart's reel read as two beats and then a break, and is the extra 15 to 60 seconds of Checking the motion worth it?
rough: Not at the bar yet: of six story requests, none reliably reads as asked at 7 or more. This pass: 7, 6, 3, 4, 5, 4 (total 49.8, the bell at 7, the first case to reach it) and, with every change in, 5, 6, 5, 4, 5, 4 (46.4); before it, 5, 6, 6, 3, 5, 4 (49.1). Those swings are within what one run differs from the next. The task stays open for it (an-animated-icon-told-as-a-little-story-moves-th).

Your trash sentence now plans in about 150 to 185 seconds (265 before), so the look sometimes runs on it and sometimes does not. When it runs, the model mostly sends the same trash keys back unchanged.

In the walk with your sentence, the plan took 194 s, past the 150 s the look waits for, so the look did not run on it; mid-play the frame shows jagged stair-step marks beside the lid's hinge that I have not explained yet.
In the heart, the crack floats loose between the halves instead of being their broken edges, and the broken heart holds for over a second before it snaps back whole.

The trash is now drawn where it is first seen, outside the can, but its path still never meets the lid, so the bounce does not read; the model was shown where every part sits at each beat and did not move it.
The envelope's letter is drawn on top of the envelope instead of behind its front, and the flap flips up into a roof shape instead of folding shut.
The new check that asks the model whether an icon moves costs about a second on every still icon whose words do not say animated.
No mock covers how Ask plans motion; this is Ask's planning, not a surface.
